- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The study aimed to identify drugs that synergize with a drug called FA in vitro.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Seven drugs were identified through a combination of checkerboard and time-kill kinetic assays.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The identified drugs include rifamycin (RIF), macrolides (ERY, CLR, ROX), oxazolidinone (LZD), aminoglycoside (STR), and an aminocyclitol class compound (SPC).
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The synergy between FA and ERY was confirmed through time-kill kinetics.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The mechanism behind the interaction between FA and ERY is not clear.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Both FA and ERY inhibit protein synthesis.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] It is possible that the combined inhibition of the translational machinery at separate processing stages is responsible for the observed whole-cell effect.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Achieving therapeutic concentrations of the drug combinations is important to prevent genetic resistance.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Cross-resistance studies were conducted to understand the potential for resistance to the synergistic drug combinations.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The study highlights promising synergistic interactions that could be further investigated against a broader panel of M. tuberculosis strains, including both drug- and multidrug-resistant clinical isolates.
